perf.summary: After the binary search lands at l, a linear scan counts matching lcp entries, degrading to O(len) when the matching interval is large.
perf.currentCost: The `for (i = l; i < len; i++)` linear count can scan up to len entries when many suffixes share the prefix length, making the function O(len) instead of O(log len) for wide intervals.
perf.proposedChange: Replace the linear forward scan with a second binary search for the last index where lcp[i] >= queryLen, then return that index - l + 1 (mirroring the existing right-bound binary search). Both bounds become O(log len).
perf.rationale: Restores O(log len) worst case for the whole query; the current linear tail dominates for common-prefix-heavy data (e.g. repetitive text), which is exactly where suffix-array locate is used.
perf.risk: Must reproduce the exact same count: the current loop counts contiguous entries from l with lcp>=queryLen, so the upper-bound binary search must use the identical comparison (>=) and inclusive bounds. Verify off-by-one against the loop on edge cases (l==len-1, all-match, none-match).
